title: Twilio webhook signature bypass with ngrok loopback compatibility enabled
summary: A configuration-specific bypass allows forged requests to a Twilio voice-call webhook to be accepted without a valid X-Twilio-Signature. The issue is not enabled by default.
ai_role: Endor Labs’ case-specific report describes its AI SAST engine’s trace for this finding and the researcher’s subsequent validation with a proof of concept. This supports AI-assisted discovery with human validation; the specific model is not named. The six-case article was updated after initial publication, so the exact first public date of its current attribution text is not established.
classification_note: The upstream security advisory documents the public disclosure and fix. The sources do not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: OpenClaw 2026.2.14 and later are listed as patched; the ngrok compatibility option no longer bypasses signature verification.

impacts.conditions: Only the described optional voice-call/ngrok configuration with public or otherwise reachable webhook exposure.
impacts.exploitation: The sources report validation or describe attack conditions but do not report observed exploitation.
